pumac-2013-finals-a-01.title: AM-GM, then a tangent line estimate
pumac-2013-finals-a-01.body:
**Step 1.** By AM-GM, $6ab\le3a^2+3b^2$, so using $a^2+b^2=1-c^2$,
$$\frac1{6ab+c^2}\ge\frac1{3a^2+3b^2+c^2}=\frac1{3-2c^2},$$
and similarly for the other two terms. So the right side is at least $\sum\frac1{3-2x_i}$ where $x_1=a^2,x_2=b^2,x_3=c^2$, $x_i>0$, $\sum x_i=1$ (so each $x_i<1$).

**Step 2.** We show $\sum\frac1{3-2x_i}\ge\sum\frac1{2+x_i}$, the left side of the claim. Let $g(x)=\frac1{3-2x}-\frac1{2+x}=\frac{3x-1}{(3-2x)(2+x)}$. We claim, for $0<x<1$,
$$g(x)\ge\frac{27}{49}\Big(x-\frac13\Big).$$
Indeed,
$$g(x)-\frac{27}{49}\Big(x-\frac13\Big)=(3x-1)\left[\frac1{(3-2x)(2+x)}-\frac9{49}\right]=\frac{(3x-1)\,(49-9(6-x-2x^2))}{49(3-2x)(2+x)}=\frac{(3x-1)^2(6x+5)}{49(3-2x)(2+x)}\ge0,$$
because $(3-2x)(2+x)=6-x-2x^2$ and $49-9(6-x-2x^2)=18x^2+9x-5=(3x-1)(6x+5)$.

Summing over the three variables: $\sum g(x_i)\ge\frac{27}{49}\big(\sum x_i-1\big)=0$. Combined with Step 1 this proves the inequality. $\blacksquare$

pumac-2013-finals-a-02.title: Similar triangles through $M$
pumac-2013-finals-a-02.body:
Let $M=AI\cap EF$. Since $AE=AF$ and $IE=IF$, line $AI$ is the perpendicular bisector of $EF$, so $IM\perp EF$ and $M$ is the foot of the altitude from $E$ in the right triangle $AEI$ (right angle at $E$). Hence
$$IM\cdot IA=IE^2=ID^2=ID'^2=r^2.$$
So $\frac{IM}{ID}=\frac{ID}{IA}$ and with the common angle at $I$, $\triangle IDM\sim\triangle IAD$, giving $\angle IDM=\angle IAD$. In the same way $\triangle ID'M\sim\triangle IAD'$ and $\angle ID'M=\angle IAD'$. Because $I$ lies on segment $DD'$, it lies inside angle $DAD'$, so
$$\angle DAD'=\angle DAI+\angle IAD'=\angle IDM+\angle ID'M.$$

**Cyclic quadrilaterals.** $\angle IDP=90^\circ$ (tangent) and $\angle IMP=90^\circ$ ($P$ is on line $EF\perp AI$), so $D$ and $M$ lie on the circle with diameter $IP$; hence $\angle IDM=\angle IPM$. Likewise $\angle ID'Q=\angle IMQ=90^\circ$ gives $\angle ID'M=\angle IQM$.

**Finish.** $P$ and $Q$ lie on line $EF$ on opposite sides of the foot $M$ of the perpendicular from $I$ (they lie on the two parallel tangents at the ends of a diameter), so in triangle $IPQ$ the angles at $P$ and $Q$ are $\angle IPM$ and $\angle IQM$. Therefore
$$\angle DAD'=\angle IPM+\angle IQM=180^\circ-\angle PIQ,$$
i.e. $\angle PIQ+\angle DAD'=180^\circ$. $\blacksquare$

pumac-2013-finals-a-03.title: Greedy matching
pumac-2013-finals-a-03.body:
Assume $G$ has no star of size $k$ (otherwise done), so every vertex has degree at most $k-1$. If $k=1$ there is an edge (so a star of size $1$), so let $k\ge2$.

Choose any edge $e_1=u_1v_1$ and delete $e_1$ together with all edges sharing an endpoint with it. Each of $u_1,v_1$ has at most $k-2$ other edges, so at most $1+2(k-2)=2k-3$ edges are deleted. Repeat in the remaining graph: choose $e_2$, delete it and all edges adjacent to it (at most $2k-3$ edges), and so on.

After $j$ steps at most $j(2k-3)$ edges have been deleted. As long as $j\le k-1$, the number of remaining edges is at least $|E|-(k-1)(2k-3)>2(k-1)^2-(k-1)(2k-3)=k-1>0$ at the start of each step $j\le k-1$, and after $k-1$ steps there is still at least one edge left, $e_k$. Every chosen edge was still present after the deletions caused by the previous choices, so $e_1,\dots,e_k$ are pairwise non-adjacent: a matching of size $k$. $\blacksquare$
